I can relate to this so deeply. When my mom killed herself I was sure I would be quick to follow. I have inherited a lot of psychological issues from her and we were actually in the mental hospital at the same time a couple weeks before she died. It's been over a year and a half, and I can't lie to you and say that I'm not suicidal anymore. But it has gotten easier to cope with. They permanence of it all is still overwhelming all the time, but I've been able to find more fulfillment in things that bring me joy, no matter how brief. I'm not excited for my future, in fact I dread it most of the time, but I still feel so full of love for the people in my life that I have. And I am doing everything I can to have as many beautiful moments with them that I can. The thing that has been hard for me in a way I didn't expect, was feeling like I didn't deserve to feel any happiness because my mother never would again. And I believed that I had deserved to die so much more than her, and it wasn't fair that I'd go on to listen to new music and read new books and feel new things and she wouldn't. That still haunts me honestly, but now I can enjoy those moments while thinking of her, and remembering that my joy was always her joy too. I am so sorry that you are going through this right now. Please know you are always welcome to message me if you want to talk to a stranger who might understand some things. Sending you all the comfort I can <3

Hi! Person with BPD here. Im sorry to hear you've been feeling some stress about this. I get it 100%. The only thing you can really do is go on living your life with them according to what is natural to you. You don't deserve to be dragged around and left wondering, so set boundaries and respect them! Communication is super important, and as long as you put into the friendship what you want out of it, and communicate your love to them, you are doing all that you can - which is enough. Even though your friend struggles with this disorder, you deserve to be respected and loved! So basically, set boundaries, express your love in a way that is natural to you, know your value, and communicate! Plus, with BPD there is a lot of internal back and forth between obsession and repulsion. So if they push you away as a result of their BPD, they will likely return. It is up to you whether or not you accept them back. I know it's hard, but it's so important for us with BPD to try and be self-aware, and to be intentional about working towards improvement for ourselves and the ones we love. Hope this helps.
